claims.text: GDACS's tropical cyclone report for DUJUAN-26 (event id 1001322) tracked the storm over the Northwest Pacific from 15 to 22 September 2026 with maximum sustained winds of 130 km/h, assessing an Overall Green alert for Japan (GDACS score 0.5) under its automated wind-exposure model, which estimates no population within Category 1 or higher wind zones and does not capture the storm's rainfall-driven flood and landslide impact documented separately by Japanese authorities.

description: Typhoon Dujuan, Japan's Typhoon No. 25, brought record rainfall and violent winds to eastern Japan from 20 to 23 September 2026, triggering floods and landslides across the Kanto region; a subsequent Typhoon No. 26 and frontal heavy rain added further damage, including Kumamoto Prefecture's first fatality. Japan Meteorological Agency issued a Level 5 special warning for landslides on Tokyo's Izu Oshima island on 21 September, and Chiba, Tokyo, Kanagawa and Okinawa prefectures stood up disaster response headquarters (Okinawa's was dissolved 28 September and Kanagawa's on 2 October). Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency's latest situation report (No. 24, 4 October) holds the toll at 17 deaths -- ten in Chiba, five in Kanagawa, one in Kumamoto and one in Miyazaki -- and now puts the missing count at zero, after the Nagara-machi, Chiba landslide victim recovered earlier was confirmed to be the same person already counted among the dead rather than an additional fatality; 41 injured and 2,412 homes damaged or destroyed are unchanged from the prior report. Evacuation instructions remain at 484 households (1,029 people) in Chiba and Kanagawa.

impact.summary: Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency's situation report No. 24 (4 October 2026, 14:00 JST) holds the toll at 17 deaths (Chiba 10, Kanagawa 5, Kumamoto 1, Miyazaki 1) and now records 0 people missing, after the one remaining missing person -- the Nagara-machi, Chiba landslide victim recovered earlier -- was confirmed to be the same individual already counted among the dead rather than an additional fatality. 41 injured (3 serious, 38 minor) and 2,412 homes damaged or destroyed (67 total collapse, 414 half collapse, 424 flooded above floor, 1,259 flooded below floor, 248 partially damaged) are unchanged from report No. 23. Evacuation instructions remain at 484 households (1,029 people) -- 464 households (996 people) in Chiba and 20 households (33 people) in Kanagawa; Kanagawa's disaster response headquarters remains dissolved since 2 October.

name: Typhoon Dujuan (Typhoon No. 25), Japan

updates.text: FDMA's report No. 24 (4 Oct, 14:00 JST) clarified that the one remaining missing person -- a Nagara-machi, Chiba landslide victim -- is the same individual already counted among the 17 confirmed deaths, not an additional fatality; missing now stands at 0. Deaths, injured, homes damaged and evacuation instructions are all unchanged from report No. 23.

FDMA's report No. 23 (3 Oct, 16:00 JST) raised the toll to 17 deaths after a Nagara-machi, Chiba landslide victim previously missing was recovered dead, cutting missing to 1; injured held at 41 and homes damaged rose to 2,412 (from 2,319). Evacuation instructions eased to 484 households (1,029 people), down from 502 (1,049); Kanagawa's disaster HQ was dissolved 2 October.

FDMA's report No. 22 (2 Oct, 8:00 JST) held deaths at 16, missing at 2 and injured at 41, all unchanged; homes damaged rose to 2,319 (from 2,211). Evacuation instructions were scaled back to 502 households (1,049 people) in Chiba/Kanagawa, down sharply from 1,315 households (2,675 people).

FDMA's report No. 21 (1 Oct, 9:00 JST) held deaths at 16 and missing at 2, both unchanged; homes damaged rose to 2,211 (from 2,180). Evacuation instructions held steady at 1,315 households (2,675 people) in Chiba and Kanagawa.

FDMA's report No. 20 (30 Sept, 9:00 JST) held deaths at 16 but missing fell to 2 (from 3); injured rose to 41 (from 38) and homes damaged to 2,180 (from 1,871). Fresh heavy rain widened evacuation instructions to 5 municipalities, 1,315 households (2,675 people) in Chiba/Kanagawa, up sharply from 502 households (1,049 people); Okinawa's disaster HQ was dissolved 28 September.

FDMA's report No. 19 (29 Sept, combining Typhoon No. 25, Typhoon No. 26 and frontal rain) raised the toll to 16 deaths, including Kumamoto Prefecture's first fatality; missing fell to 3 and homes damaged rose to 1,871. The large Kumamoto/Saga heavy-rain evacuation instructions from 27 Sept were lifted, leaving about 1,049 people still under evacuation instructions in Chiba and Kanagawa.

FDMA's report No. 17 (27 Sept) raised the toll to 13 deaths and 4 missing; homes damaged surged to 1,710 as Ibaraki/Saitama were added. Separate 27 Sept heavy-rain warnings triggered mass evacuation instructions in Kumamoto (~828,500) and Saga (~7,600).

FDMA's situation report No. 13 (24 September, 17:00 JST) raised the toll to 12 deaths (3 disaster-related; Chiba 7, Kanagawa 4, Miyazaki 1) and damaged homes to 828, while missing fell to 3 (Kamogawa, Nagara-machi and Miura landslides) and injured fell to 28. Evacuation instructions held steady at 509 households (1,062 people) in Chiba and Kanagawa.

FDMA's situation report No. 10 (23 September, 12:00 JST) raised the toll to 10 deaths (Chiba 6, Kanagawa 3, Miyazaki 1) and 42 injured, with 4 still missing from landslides in Kamogawa, Yokosuka and Miura; damaged homes rose to 659. Evacuation instructions were scaled back to about 1,062 people, down from a 21-22 September peak of 74,289.

FDMA's situation report No. 8 (22 September, 12:30 JST) recorded 5 deaths, 3 missing and 468 damaged homes; evacuation instructions covered 74,289 people across Chiba, Tokyo and Kanagawa. Tokyo's Oshima Town had been placed under a Level 5 landslide special warning on 21 September, downgraded to Level 4 by 23:00 the same day.
